findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Testing / Verification step describing how primary-source OSS prior art and design gotchas are gathered and recorded as a research comment with cited URLs.
evidence: The Testing / Verification section enumerates benchmarks, extraction, fixture assertions, and recording of 'command output, timestamps, environment facts, and cleanup outcome' but never mentions gathering OSS prior art or producing a research comment with cited URLs.
This AC is thereby an orphan criterion with no described step producing its evidence.
findings.finding: The acceptance criterion requiring primary-source OSS prior art and cited URLs has no covering step in Testing / Verification.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Primary-source OSS prior art and design gotchas are recorded on this ticket; checked by cited URLs in the research comment.'
scenarios: Executor completes all benchmark/fixture work but has no described task to surface the research comment, leaving this AC unverifiable against the plan body.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a verification bullet: 'Collect primary-source OSS prior art on pinned read-only Git views (e.g., libgit2/gitoxide docs, Git plumbing man pages) and record cited URLs plus design gotchas as a research comment on this ticket.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define AC-3's comparison as like-with-like: reduce both the pinned extraction and a single-dir copy of the same live ticket directory (identical tracker_dir sibling context), or state that alias-form LINK targets are absent for the chosen ticket, so alias→canonical resolution cannot cause a false hash divergence.
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:242-253 resolve_ticket_id needs sibling dirs to canonicalize alias-form LINK targets; falls back to verbatim otherwise
Plan compares 'a scoped pinned directory' to 'the captured live directory' but does not pin down whether the live side is an isolated single-dir copy or an in-store reduce
findings.finding: AC-3's canonical-hash equality assertion via reduce_ticket may compare unlike states: reduce_ticket derives tracker_dir from the ticket dir's parent and resolves alias-form LINK targets to canonical UUIDs only when sibling ticket dirs are present, so an isolated pinned-extraction of ONE directory (no siblings) can produce different deps[].target_id values than a full in-store reduce.
findings.location: Testing/Verification (reduce_ticket equality) and AC line 'A scoped pinned directory reduces to the same canonical target-state hash as the captured live directory'
scenarios: A ticket with alias-form depends_on links reduces to divergent deps in the isolated extraction vs. the full live store, causing a false hash mismatch (or masking a real one)
findings.suggested_fix: Pick a ticket whose LINK targets are already canonical UUIDs (or extract enough sibling dirs to make resolution symmetric), and specify that both sides run reduce_ticket with equivalent tracker_dir context.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that reduce_ticket comparisons exclude or neutralize the reducer cache (e.g. strip/ignore .cache.json before reducing, or compare only the reduced state dict) so the cache write side-effect cannot mutate the read-only target or serve a stale reduce.
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:220-221 calls write_cache(cache_path, dir_hash, result, ticket_dir) on the non-override path
A .cache.json blob may also be present in the pinned Git tree and get extracted, biasing a subsequent reduce
findings.finding: reduce_ticket writes a .cache.json into the ticket directory as a side effect; the plan's byte-identity / equality assertions do not account for this cache write, which mutates the 'read-only' live directory being compared and can perturb byte-parity or reflect a stale cached reduce.
findings.location: Testing/Verification (reduce_ticket equality; 'reads through A remain byte-identical') and AC lines for canonical-hash and byte-identity
scenarios: Running reduce_ticket against the live captured directory writes .cache.json, mutating the supposedly read-only comparison target
A pinned tree containing a stale .cache.json is extracted and short-circuits reduce_ticket to a cached (possibly divergent) result
